name: Does compressing a PDF upload my file?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Compression happens entirely in your browser using JavaScript. Your PDF is never uploaded to any server or sent over the internet. You can verify this yourself: open your browser's DevTools → Network tab during compression — you should not see your PDF being uploaded to a remote server.

name: Will compression reduce the visual quality of my PDF?

acceptedAnswer.text: PDFree offers three presets. Light removes only metadata — text and images are completely untouched. Standard recompresses images at 82% JPEG quality — quality loss is minimal and not visible in most documents. Maximum recompresses at 72% — noticeable only on close inspection of photo-heavy PDFs.

name: How much can PDFree reduce a PDF file size?

acceptedAnswer.text: Typical reductions are 20–70%. PDFs with high-resolution images (scanned documents, photo brochures) compress the most — often 50–80% savings. Text-only PDFs see less reduction since text is already stored efficiently as vectors.

name: Why does the compressed PDF look the same but is smaller?

acceptedAnswer.text: PDFs often contain invisible bloat: page thumbnails generated by Adobe Reader, duplicate embedded fonts, XMP metadata streams, embedded color profiles, and PieceInfo private data from Adobe applications. PDFree removes these hidden extras. The visible content — text, images, layout — remains identical.

name: Can I compress a password-protected PDF?

acceptedAnswer.text: PDFree attempts to optimize encrypted PDFs when possible, but strongly protected files may not compress fully. For best results, remove the password first using the PDFree Protect PDF tool (which can also remove existing passwords), then compress.

name: Does PDF compression work without an internet connection?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. PDFree works fully offline as a Progressive Web App once the page has loaded. No internet connection is required — all processing runs in your browser.

name: Can I compress a PDF to send by email?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — that is the most common use case. Most email providers cap attachments at 25MB. Choose the Standard preset to compress your PDF for email: it typically reduces file size 30–50% with no visible quality loss. If the file is still too large, try the Maximum preset, which can cut size by 50–80% at the cost of some image sharpness.

name: Is this PDF compressor completely free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. PDFree is a completely free PDF compressor — no subscription, no sign up, no watermarks on the output. Compress as many PDFs as you need with no daily limit and no file size cap.
